numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Angle("1d2m59.49999s").to_string(precision=0) gives "1d03m00s" (seconds carried into the next minute half a unit too early). Angle("285d29m41.76s").to_string(fields=1) gives "286d" (seconds rounded into minutes before minutes rounded into degrees, rounding twice).
trigger_conditions: precision=0 with seconds just below the half-unit rounding boundary (e.g. 59.49999s)
fields=1 with minutes and seconds that round up across the degree boundary (e.g. 285d29m41.76s)

numerical_characteristics.precision: The rounding depends on the precision argument: ndp = 8 when precision is None, otherwise the given precision. Tests use precision 0, 1 and 2 for seconds, and fields=1 for degrees.
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Carry boundary cases: seconds near 59.5 carrying into minutes and degrees (e.g. 1d2m59.49999s vs 1d2m59.5s), and degrees near 285 where minutes rounding must not double-round (e.g. 285d29m41.76s).
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: Half a unit in the last displayed digit: seconds at or above that threshold carry, below it do not. For fields=1, 30 minutes (half a degree) is the carry threshold.
category_specific_evidence: Changelog: Angle.to_string carried seconds into minutes half a unit too early, giving 1d03m00s instead of 1d02m59s for Angle('1d2m59.49999s').to_string(precision=0).
Changelog: with fields=1 seconds were rounded into minutes before minutes into degrees (double rounding), giving 286d instead of 285d for Angle('285d29m41.76s').to_string(fields=1).
Source comment: builtin round is used instead of NumPy round because NumPy disagrees with the formatting on ties.
New code rounds seconds with round(float(values[2]), ndp) only when fields == 3.
Regression tests cover precision 0, 1 and 2 for seconds rounding and fields=1 degree rounding, including negative angles.
Tests cover the boundary at exactly 30 minutes (285d30m gives 286d) and just below it (285d29m59.9s gives 285d).
The passages do not state a dtype or floating-point width for the discrepancy, so dtype is null.
reproduction_risks: Tie behaviour differs between builtin round and NumPy round, so tie cases at exactly half a unit may diverge across implementations.
Double rounding appears only with fields=1 and values near the half-degree boundary; the evidence does not show it for other field settings.
No dtype or floating-point width is stated, so a dtype-dependent reproduction cannot be confirmed from the passages.
The buggy commit (bdd570d53507) and PR date are not given in the passages, so the pre-fix version cannot be pinned from them.
